title: Electrolysis
lead: An external power source can impose a voltage on a redox system and drive a reaction that would not take place on its own. This section follows electrolysis through molten sodium chloride, water and aqueous sodium chloride, shows it at work in electroplating, and counts the electrons it moves from the current and the time.
objectives: Compare the operation of electrolytic cells with that of galvanic cells
Perform stoichiometric calculations for electrolytic processes
summary_html: Nonspontaneous redox processes may be forced to occur in electrochemical cells by the application of an appropriate potential using an external power source—a process known as electrolysis. Electrolysis is the basis for certain ore refining processes, the industrial production of many chemical commodities, and the electroplating of metal coatings on various products. Measurement of the current flow during electrolysis permits stoichiometric calculations.

exercises.prompt: Aluminum metal can be made from aluminum(III) ions by electrolysis. What is the half-reaction at the cathode? What mass of aluminum metal would be recovered if a current of 25.0 A passed through the solution for 15.0 minutes?

answer.hint: Each Al3+ ion takes three electrons, so the moles of aluminum are one third of It/F.

exercises.prompt: What mass of zinc is required to galvanize the top of a 3.00 m × 5.50 m sheet of iron to a thickness of 0.100 mm of zinc? If the zinc comes from a solution of Zn(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub> and the current is 25.5 A, how long will it take to galvanize the top of the iron? The density of zinc is 7.140 g/cm<sup>3</sup>.

parts.hint: The volume of zinc is the area of the top times the thickness; its density gives the mass.
Each Zn2+ ion takes two electrons; t = Q/I.

exercises.prompt: What mass of each product is produced in each of the electrolytic cells of the previous problem if a total charge of 3.33 × 10<sup>5</sup> C passes through each cell? The previous problem electrolyzes each of these molten salts: (a) CaCl<sub>2</sub>, (b) LiH, (c) AlCl<sub>3</sub>, (d) CrBr<sub>3</sub>.

answer.solution: (a) mass Ca = 69.1 g, mass Cl<sub>2</sub> = 122 g; (b) mass Li = 23.9 g, mass H<sub>2</sub> = 3.48 g; (c) mass Al = 31.0 g, mass Cl<sub>2</sub> = 122 g; (d) mass Cr = 59.8 g, mass Br<sub>2</sub> = 276 g
